text:
marina: Heads-up — noticed a small class of inference pods landing on the standard nodepool (no GPUs) even though we taint gpu pools with redwood.com/gpu=present:NoSchedule. This started after yesterday's autoscaler config change.

samir: :eyes: are those pods missing the toleration or are the nodes missing the taint?

marina: quick grep shows node taints intact: `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{": "}{.spec.taints}{"
"}{end}' | grep gpu` returns multiple nodes with `redwood.com/gpu=present:NoSchedule`. Pod spec shows no tolerations. Example snippet from the failing job: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: replayer spec: containers: - name: replayer image: replayer:prod command: ["/bin/run"] resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: 1```

jia: ah, that is the issue — requesting GPU resource doesn't automatically grant scheduling onto tainted nodes if the pod lacks the toleration when taint uses key/value form. We historically used taint `redwood.com/gpu:NoSchedule` (no value) but we migrated to a key=value taint for better pool differentiation. Some older job templates still assume implicit behavior.

samir: ok, two fixes: (1) add the toleration to job templates, or (2) change taint to value-less form to preserve backward compat. I prefer (1) since we want pool labels for multi-GPU vs single-GPU. Example toleration to add: ```yaml tolerations: - key: "redwood.com/gpu" operator: "Equal" value: "present" effect: "NoSchedule"```

marina: adding toleration + nodeAffinity to prefer GPU pool is safer: ```yaml nodeSelector: node.redwood.com/pool: gpu-pool nodeAffinity: requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: nodeSelectorTerms: - matchExpressions: - key: node.redwood.com/pool operator: In values: - gpu-pool``` That avoids accidental scheduling to other pools even if autoscaler mixes labels.

ops-bot: FYI — autoscaler change was rolling out yesterday: switched expander from "most-pods" to "least-waste" and enabled nodeGroup auto-discovery for the clustered GPU ASGs. Might be related.

samir: important note — cluster-autoscaler can introduce race windows where it brings up gen nodes while a GPU node group is still spinning up, and the scheduler will place pods on gen nodes if toleration is missing. Also mixed-instance taints can be inherited when using mixed-ASG labels.

marina: running a quick fix patch to the runner templates in k8s-manifests repo to include toleration + affinity, pushing now. Will roll a canary to replayer jobs.

jia: also consider adding a validating webhook to reject Pod specs that request nvidia.com/gpu without the required toleration/affinity. Saves on noisy failures. We can implement a simple check in devex repo.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0320-17 — pods mis-scheduled to non-GPU nodes; priority: low (workaround available).

samir: long-term: we should document the taint schema (key/value vs key-only) in infra runbook and add migration notes. Also audit cronjobs and k8s templates for missing tolerations. I can run a query to find all pods requesting GPUs without tolerations.

marina: perfect. I'll watch canary and report back. Thanks. :thumbsup:
